tasks.gr7-poem-writing-t1: Topic: Writing a poem (Grade 7 English Home Language, Term 1). Cover lines, stanzas, the quatrain, end rhyme and rhyme schemes (AABB), imagery, the figures of speech simile, metaphor, personification, alliteration and onomatopoeia, rhythm, free verse, the title, and the writing process (plan, draft, revise, edit, present). Use original examples only and no quoted poem. Ask Grade 7 learners to identify the features and figures of speech with exactly one correct option.
tasks.gr7-drama-dialogue-t1: Topic: Writing a dialogue for drama (Grade 7 English Home Language, Term 1). Cover the format of a script (setting, the character name and a colon at the start of each line, no quotation marks, a new line for each speaker), stage directions in brackets, showing character and point of view through speech, short natural lines, and enacting and checking a scene (beginning, middle and end). Use invented characters. Ask Grade 7 learners to identify the parts and set out lines with exactly one correct option.
tasks.gr7-instructions-t2: Topic: Writing instructions (Grade 7 English Home Language, Term 2). Cover the title, the materials list, numbered steps in order, command verbs (imperatives), sequence words (first, next, then, finally), the present tense, exact amounts, times and tools, warnings, and testing the instructions with a friend. Ask Grade 7 learners to identify the features and choose the clearest step with exactly one correct option.
tasks.gr7-drama-review-t2: Topic: Writing a drama review (Grade 7 English Home Language, Term 2). Cover the parts of a review (details of the play, a short summary without the ending, comments on the acting and the staging, an opinion with reasons, a recommendation), supporting comments with examples, balance, linking words (because, although), present tense for the plot, and the order of the paragraphs. Use an invented play. Ask Grade 7 learners to identify and choose the best part with exactly one correct option.
tasks.gr7-forms-questionnaires-t3: Topic: Forms and questionnaires (Grade 7 English Home Language, Term 3). Cover reading all the instructions, block letters, writing the date as dd/mm/yyyy, ticking one box, giving a full name and correct contact details, closed and open questions and rating scales in a questionnaire, clear one-idea questions, the declaration, the signature, a parent or guardian signing for a young person, and a final check. Use invented details only. Ask Grade 7 learners to complete and judge forms and questions with exactly one correct option.
tasks.gr7-notice-agenda-minutes-t3: Topic: Notice, agenda and minutes (Grade 7 English Home Language, Term 3). Cover a notice (heading, what, when, where, who issued it, date), an agenda (a numbered list of items in order, sent before a meeting: welcome and apologies, minutes of the last meeting, matters to discuss, other business, closure), minutes (the record of a meeting written afterwards in the past tense: who was present, what was discussed and decided, who must act) and choosing the right text. Use invented groups. Ask Grade 7 learners to identify and choose the right text with exactly one correct option.
tasks.gr7-newspaper-article-t3: Topic: Writing a newspaper article (Grade 7 English Home Language, Term 3). Cover the headline, the by-line, the lead paragraph answering who, what, where, when, why and how, the body in order of importance (inverted pyramid), the third person and the past tense, direct and reported quotations with attribution, neutral language and accurate facts. Use invented names. Ask Grade 7 learners to identify the parts and choose the best lead or headline with exactly one correct option.
tasks.gr7-diary-email-flyer-t4: Topic: Diary entry, e-mail and flyer (Grade 7 English Home Language, Term 4). Cover the diary entry (date, Dear Diary, first person, events and feelings, informal), the e-mail (To, Cc, a clear subject, a greeting, short paragraphs, a closing, a formal and polite register for an adult) and the flyer (a bold heading, key facts what, when, where and cost, a short message, contact details), and matching the register to the reader. Use invented details. Ask Grade 7 learners to identify and choose with exactly one correct option.
tasks.gr7-speech-t4: Topic: Writing and giving a speech (Grade 7 English Home Language, Term 4). Cover the opening, body and closing of a speech, audience and purpose (inform, persuade, entertain), the register, techniques (rhetorical question, repetition, the rule of three, a personal story), the writing process, practising aloud, and delivery (clear voice, eye contact, posture, cue cards). Ask Grade 7 learners to identify the parts and techniques with exactly one correct option.
